title: Noodle missing from Generation trigger filter values
reality: v2.3.4 added Noodle to Lorebook entry Generation filters (#3842): entries can set generationTriggerFilters to target Noodle timeline-refresh context specifically, without leaking into chat/continue/autonomous or other generation paths. The file's trigger list only says 'chat, continue, autonomous, etc.' and the v2.2 Noodle note implies Noodle participation is only controllable via the chat-level opt-in Lorebook context setting, not per-entry.
fix: Add Noodle to the enumerated trigger values with a (v2.3.4, #3842) note; cross-reference from the Noodle paragraph in the Scope section as the way to scope individual entries to Noodle.

title: Semantic matches now share keyword matches' context-budget priority
reality: v2.3.4 gave current semantic (vector) lorebook matches the same context-budget priority as current keyword matches, so configured entry order — not activation method — decides which entries fit. Previously semantic activations were deprioritized behind keyword activations in budgeting.
fix: Add a (v2.3.4) note to 'Token Budget Management' (and/or the v2.2 vector-fallback paragraph): semantically-activated entries compete for tokenBudget on equal footing with keyword-activated ones — entry order decides which entries are attached when over budget, regardless of activation method.

title: Lorebook entry content now reaches the model verbatim (no HTML escaping)
reality: v2.3.4 stopped HTML-escaping angle brackets in prompt leaf content: lorebook entry content now reaches the model verbatim instead of arriving as <thinking>. Finalizes leaf content as verbatim; supersedes the earlier #3108 escaping and untrusted-card-text escaping; framework structural wrappers and agent value/attribute XML escapers unchanged. Authors have no guidance that inline HTML/XML in entry content is now delivered literally.
fix: Add a (v2.3.4) note near the content field description or in Best Practices → Entry length: entry content is injected verbatim — angle brackets and inline HTML/XML are passed exactly as written; entries may deliberately contain markup like <scenario> blocks.

title: Roleplay Active Context lorebook details now at parity with Conversation/Game
reality: v2.3.4 (#3840) matched Roleplay's Active Context lorebook details to Conversation and Game: activation sources, matched keys, semantic scores, current-location grouping, budget skips, and expandable entry content. The file only describes the World Info Inspector with 'token usage and keyword reasons'.
fix: Update the World Info Inspector / UI Location bullet: (v2.3.4, #3840) Active Context lorebook details are consistent across Conversation, Game, and Roleplay with the full diagnostic set.

title: Embedded-lorebook data now survives partial Character PATCH and card validation
reality: v2.3.4 fixed two embedded-lorebook data-loss paths: partial nested Character PATCHes deep-merge without materializing destructive defaults (#3858), and native card validation/normalization preserves unknown embedded-lorebook properties (#3859). Prior versions could silently drop embedded-lorebook data on partial character updates.
fix: Append to the 'Character Lorebook tab' bullet: (v2.3.4) embedded-lorebook data is preserved through partial Character PATCH requests (deep-merge, #3858), and card validation keeps unknown embedded-lorebook properties intact (#3859) — imported cards with nonstandard embedded-lorebook fields no longer lose them.
